claim: The manuscript presents an integrated neuro-histological pipeline for systematic mesoscale connectivity mapping in the common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus).
source: Here we present an integrated neuro-histological pipeline as well as a grid-based tracer injection strategy for systematic mesoscale connectivity mapping in the common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus).
evidence: The abstract directly states the development of the pipeline.

claim: Individual marmoset brains are sectioned into approximately 1700 20 µm sections using the tape transfer technique.
source: Individual brains are sectioned into ~1700 20 µm sections using the tape transfer technique, permitting high quality 3D reconstruction of a series of histochemical stains (Nissl, myelin) interleaved with tracer labeled sections.
evidence: The abstract describes the sectioning methodology and section count.

claim: The tape transfer technique permits high quality 3D reconstruction of histochemical stains and tracer labeled sections.

evidence: The abstract states that the tape transfer technique enables high quality 3D reconstruction.

claim: Systematic in-vivo MRI of individual animals facilitates injection placement into reference-atlas defined anatomical compartments.

evidence: The abstract describes the use of in-vivo MRI for guiding injections.

claim: The integrated computational pipeline enables accurate mapping of individual brains into a common reference atlas despite significant individual variation.
source: Further, by combining the resulting 3D volumes, containing informative cytoarchitectonic markers, with in-vivo and ex-vivo MRI, and using an integrated computational pipeline, we are able to accurately map individual brains into a common reference atlas despite the significant individual variation.
evidence: The abstract states that the computational pipeline achieves accurate mapping despite individual variation.

source: All experimental procedures were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee at RIKEN and a field work license from Monash University, and conducted in accordance with the Guidelines for Conducting Animal Experiments at RIKEN Center for Brain Science and the Australian Code of Practice for the Care and Use of Animals for Scientific Purposes.
evidence: The Materials and methods section states ethical approval.

claim: Female marmosets (Callithrix jacchus), 4 to 8 years old, 330 g - 440 g in weight, were used in the study.
source: Female marmosets (Callithrix jacchus), 4 to 8 years old, 330 g - 440 g in weight, were acquired from the Japanese Central Institute for Experimental Animals.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the animals used.

claim: MR scans were performed using a 9.4T BioSpec 94/30 US/R MRI scanner.
source: MR scans were performed using a 9.4T BioSpec 94/30 US/R MRI scanner (Bruker, Biospin, Ettlingen, Germany) with actively shielded gradients that had a maximum strength of 660 mT/m.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the MRI equipment.

claim: Four tracers were placed in the right hemisphere of each marmoset.
source: To conserve animals, four tracers were placed in the right hemisphere of each marmoset, including two anterograde tracers: AAV-TRE3-tdTomato (AAV-tdTOM) and AAV-TRE3-Clover (AAV-GFP), and two retrograde tracers: Fast Blue (FB) and CTB.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the tracer injection strategy.

claim: Two anterograde tracers used were AAV-TRE3-tdTomato (AAV-tdTOM) and AAV-TRE3-Clover (AAV-GFP).
source: To conserve animals, four tracers were placed in the right hemisphere of each marmoset, including two anterograde tracers: AAV-TRE3-tdTomato (AAV-tdTOM) and AAV-TRE3-Clover (AAV-GFP), and two retrograde tracers: Fast Blue (FB) and CTB.
evidence: The Materials and methods section lists the anterograde tracers.

claim: Two retrograde tracers used were Fast Blue (FB) and CTB.
source: To conserve animals, four tracers were placed in the right hemisphere of each marmoset, including two anterograde tracers: AAV-TRE3-tdTomato (AAV-tdTOM) and AAV-TRE3-Clover (AAV-GFP), and two retrograde tracers: Fast Blue (FB) and CTB.
evidence: The Materials and methods section lists the retrograde tracers.

claim: Tracers were delivered using Nanoject II with dosage controlled by Micro4.
source: Tracers were delivered at the injection sites using Nanoject II (Drummond, USA), with dosage controlled by Micro4 (WPI, USA).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the injection equipment.

claim: For cortical injections, each tracer was delivered at depths of 1200 µm, 800 µm, and 400 µm sequentially perpendicular to the cortical sheet, with equal volumes.
source: For cortical injections, each tracer was delivered with depths of 1200 µm, 800 µm, and 400 µm sequentially perpendicular to the cortical sheet, with equal volumes.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the cortical injection protocol.

claim: The current data set used to validate the method includes 118 injections.
source: The current data set used to validate the method presented here includes 118 injections.
evidence: The Materials and methods section states the number of injections in the validation data set.

claim: After tracer injection, there was a 4 week incubation period.
source: After tracer injection and a 4 week incubation period, the marmoset brain was perfused with a 0.1M phosphate buffer (PB) flush solution followed by 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in 0.1M PB fixation solution.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the incubation period.

claim: The brain was immersed in 10% then 30% sucrose solution over a 48 hr period to safeguard against thermal damage.
source: It was then immersed in 10% then 30% sucrose solution over a 48 hr period to safeguard against thermal damage.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the cryoprotection protocol.

claim: Cryo-sectioning of the brain was performed using a Leica CM3050 S Cryostat.
source: Cryo-sectioning of the brain was performed using a Leica CM3050 S Cryostat in a humidity chamber set at 18°C and 80% humidity.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the sectioning equipment.

claim: Each section was 20 μm in thickness.
source: Each section was 20 μm in thickness, hence the spacing between every two consecutive sections in the same series was 80 μm.
evidence: The Materials and methods section states the section thickness.

claim: The spacing between every two consecutive sections in the same series was 80 μm.
source: Each section was 20 μm in thickness, hence the spacing between every two consecutive sections in the same series was 80 μm.
evidence: The Materials and methods section states the spacing between sections.

claim: High-throughput Nissl staining was performed in an automated staining machine (Sakura Tissue-Tek Prisma).
source: High-throughput Nissl staining of neuron somata was performed in an automated staining machine (Sakura Tissue-Tek Prisma, DRS-Prisma-J0S) (Figure 2c).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the Nissl staining method and refers to Figure 2c.

claim: The myelin staining technique used a modified ammoniacal silver stain originally developed by Gallyas.
source: The myelin staining technique used a modified ammoniacal silver stain originally developed by Gallyas (Gallyas, 1979).
evidence: The Materials and methods section cites Gallyas, 1979 for the myelin staining method.

claim: All prepared slides were scanned by a Nanozoomer 2.0 HT using a 20x objective (0.46 μm/pixel in plane) at 12-bit depth.
source: All the prepared slides were scanned by series with a Nanozoomer 2.0 HT (Hamamatsu, Japan) using a 20x objective (0.46 μm/pixel in plane) at 12-bit depth and saved in an uncompressed RAW format.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the imaging parameters.

claim: The RAW images for all four series of slides comprise approximately 8 terabytes of data for each brain.
source: The RAW images for all four series of slides comprise ~8 terabytes of data for each brain.
evidence: The Materials and methods section states the data volume per brain.

claim: Images of individual sections were downsampled by 64 times and registered to one another using rigid-body transformation.
source: Images of individual sections were downsampled by 64 times and registered to one another using rigid-body transformation (William et al., 2011).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the registration method and cites William et al., 2011.

claim: Automatic annotation of brain structures was achieved by registering the Brain/MINDs atlas to ex-vivo MRI and then aligned to the 2D registered Nissl series.
source: Automatic annotation of the brain structures was achieved by registering the Brain/MINDs atlas to ex-vivo MRI and then aligned to the 2D registered Nissl series ('target images').
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the automatic annotation method.

claim: Large Deformation Diffeomorphic Metric Mapping (LDDMM) was used to match the atlas images to the MRI images.
source: After transformation, the atlas images was matched to the MRI images using Large Deformation Diffeomorphic Metric Mapping (LDDMM) (Ceritoglu et al., 2010) which transforms the atlas coordinate to the MRI image coordinate system.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the registration method and cites Ceritoglu et al., 2010.

claim: A data portal was developed to allow for viewing and interpreting high-resolution images online.
source: As an integral part of the computational pipeline, a data portal was developed to allow for viewing and interpreting high-resolution images online (http://marmoset.brainarchitecture.org).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the data portal.

claim: Less than one percent of total sections were excluded from 2D alignment.
source: Poor-quality sections such as sections with folding, tears, artefacts and discoloration missed from the previous QC stage were selected by visual inspection and excluded from the 2D alignment step. Less than one percent of total sections were excluded.
evidence: The Results section states the percentage of excluded sections.

claim: The degree of shrinkage is 7% from in- to ex-vivo MRI and 1% from ex-vivo MRI to histology.
source: The degree of shrinkage is 7% from in- to ex-vivo MRI and 1% from ex-vivo MRI to histology.
evidence: The Results section provides quantitative shrinkage measurements.

claim: Automatic process detection identified projection targets from V1 to various regions, including the most prominent projections detected in V5 and dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus (DLG).
source: Automatic process detection identified projection targets from V1 to various regions, including the most prominent projections detected in V5 and dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus (DLG).
evidence: The Results section describes specific projection findings.

claim: Projection targets from V6 included the lateral pulvinar (LPul) and medial pulvinar (MPul) among other targets.
source: Projection targets from V6 included the lateral pulvinar (LPul) and medial pulvinar (MPul) among other targets.
evidence: The Results section describes specific projection findings.

claim: Automatic cell detection for the Fast Blue tracer identified the regions projecting to V6 including prominent projections from A6DC, A31, and inferior pulvinar (IPul).
source: Automatic cell detection for the Fast Blue tracer identified the regions projecting to V6 including prominent projections from A6DC, A31, and inferior pulvinar (IPul).
evidence: The Results section describes specific retrograde tracing findings.

claim: The pipeline combines well-established neuroanatomical protocols with automated instrumentation and a software system for improving efficiency.
source: The pipeline combines the well-established neuroanatomical protocols with automated instrumentation and a software system for greatly improving the efficiency of the techniques compared to conventional manually-intensive processing.
evidence: The Discussion section summarizes the pipeline's approach.

claim: Access to high-quality in-vivo and ex-vivo MRI provided important auxiliary data sets facilitating re-assembly of section images and atlas mapping.
source: Access to high-quality in-vivo and the ex-vivo MRI provided us with important auxiliary data sets facilitating re-assembly of the section images and atlas mapping, thus ameliorating the challenges arising from increased individual variations in brain geometry in an NHP compared with laboratory mice.
evidence: The Discussion section describes the role of MRI data.

claim: Classical Nissl and myelin stains remain the gold standard for cytoarchitectonic texture-based determination of precise brain region location and delineation.
source: Classical Nissl and myelin stains remain the gold standard for cytoarchitectonic texture-based determination of precise brain region location and delineation.
evidence: The Discussion section states the value of classical stains.

claim: Within a sample of 26 cases, the whole brain volume had a median of 8222.5 mm³ with a median absolute deviation (MAD) of 319.4 mm³.
source: Within a sample of 26 cases, the whole brain volume had a median of 8222.5 mm3 with a median absolute deviation (MAD) of 319.4 mm3.
evidence: The Discussion section provides quantitative data on brain volume variation.

claim: The study did not find a significant relationship between whole brain volume and age or body weight within the data set.
source: We did not find a significant relationship between whole brain volume and age or body weight (see Appendix 10) within our data set.
evidence: The Discussion section reports the absence of a relationship.

claim: Some individual compartment sizes significantly departed from the template brain.
source: Nevertheless, some individual compartment sizes significantly departed from the template brain (e.g. the Hippocampal formation showed a consistently smaller size), indicating that the template brain may not be representative of a population average.
evidence: The Discussion section reports variation from the template.

claim: The Hippocampal formation showed a consistently smaller size compared to the template brain.
source: Nevertheless, some individual compartment sizes significantly departed from the template brain (e.g. the Hippocampal formation showed a consistently smaller size), indicating that the template brain may not be representative of a population average.
evidence: The Discussion section provides a specific example of variation.

claim: 73% of the injections placed are localized within atlas-determined anatomical compartments.
source: Based on a preliminary analysis, 73% of the injections placed are localized within atlas-determined anatomical compartments, whereas 27% showed some spread across boundaries.
evidence: The Discussion section provides quantitative data on injection localization.

claim: 27% of injections showed some spread across boundaries.
source: Based on a preliminary analysis, 73% of the injections placed are localized within atlas-determined anatomical compartments, whereas 27% showed some spread across boundaries.
evidence: The Discussion section provides quantitative data on injection spread.

claim: Manual analysis of a subset of 15 injections showed diameters in the range 0.8 mm-2.5mm.
source: Manual analysis of a subset of 15 injections showed diameters in the range 0.8 mm-2.5mm, indicating rough correspondence with the desired grid spacing.
evidence: The Discussion section provides quantitative data on injection sizes.

claim: Among 15 analyzed injections, six had tracer spread beyond the compartment boundary.
source: Among these 15 injections, six had tracer spread beyond the compartment boundary.
evidence: The Discussion section provides quantitative data on injection spread.

claim: For injections with spread beyond boundaries, about 68% of the volume was restrained within the same region as the injection center, while about 32% leaked outside to adjacent regions.
source: On average, for these six injections, about 68% of the volume was restrained within the same region as the injection center, while about 32% of the volume leaked outside to adjacent regions.
evidence: The Discussion section provides quantitative data on injection containment.

claim: To obtain an upper bound for brain-wide coverage, a cutoff of 0.8 mm³ corresponds to 356 sites (712 injections).
source: To obtain an upper bound, we assume a cutoff of 0.8 mm^3 (corresponding to the smallest injections we placed so far), which corresponds to 356 sites (712 injections).
evidence: The Discussion section provides estimates for completing brain-wide coverage.

claim: So far, 190 injections have been placed in 49 brains.
source: So far, 190 injections have been placed in 49 brains.
evidence: The Discussion section states the current progress.

claim: To cover the rest of the brain, 264 more injections would be placed in the cortex, and 258 injections in subcortical regions and cerebellum.
source: To cover the rest of the brain, 264 more injections would be placed in the cortex, and 258 injections in subcortical regions and cerebellum.
evidence: The Discussion section provides estimates for remaining work.

claim: Completing the remaining injections would require 131 brains.
source: This would require 131 brains.
evidence: The Discussion section provides estimates for animal requirements.

claim: The current pipeline has achieved a maximum capacity of 2 brains/month.
source: The current pipeline has achieved a maximum capacity of 2 brains/month.
evidence: The Discussion section states the pipeline throughput.

claim: At the current rate, a complete marmoset mesoscale connectivity map would be available by 2024.
source: At this rate, a complete marmoset mesoscale connectivity map would be available by 2024.
evidence: The Discussion section projects a completion timeline.

claim: The pipeline can be generalized to 2 × 3 inch slides, which can handle larger brains such as that of macaque.
source: The pipeline can be generalized in the future to 2 × 3 inch slides, which can handle larger brains (such as that of macaque), with a few technical innovations, importantly in stainers/coverslippers for the larger format slides.
evidence: The Discussion section speculates about future applications.
